questions.q: Per this lesson's closing argument, what are most recurring application architecture mistakes actually failures of?
options: Not knowing that a specific Salesforce feature exists
Using too many custom objects in every project
Failing to apply a known process or discipline under real-world pressure, such as a deadline or an eager stakeholder, rather than a knowledge gap
Lacking access to Salesforce's official documentation
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames these mistakes as process failures under pressure, not failures to know a fact -- every mistake on the list ties back to a discipline the course already taught.

questions.q: Which of these is listed in this lesson as a recurring mistake tied back to Lesson 6 and Lesson 9?
options: Multiple triggers on one object with no handler pattern, and Flow sprawl with no naming convention
Choosing a standard object instead of a custom object
Using an unlocked package instead of a managed package
Writing an ADR-style decision record for a significant choice
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties uncontrolled trigger proliferation and undocumented Flow sprawl back to Lesson 6's one-trigger-per-object pattern and Lesson 9's maintainability discipline.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe 'premature abstraction's various disguises' as a recurring mistake?
options: Always avoiding any form of code reuse under any circumstances
Only ever building fully custom solutions instead of configuring standard features
Refusing to ever document a design decision
Building generic, reusable, or future-proofed structures before a second real use case or a plausible signaled need actually justifies them
questions.explain: This ties back to Lessons 10 and 14 -- building speculative flexibility or reuse before it's demonstrated by a real second use case or a genuinely signaled future need.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend using the consolidated mistake list as a fast pre-build and pre-review pass, rather than just reading it once?
options: Because the list contains new information not covered anywhere else in the course

Because none of these mistakes are a surprise by this point -- running down the list takes a few minutes and catches the same categories of mistake that tend to resurface project after project regardless of individual skill
Because Salesforce requires this checklist to be submitted before certification
Because the list replaces the need for design review entirely
questions.explain: The lesson argues the value is in turning already-known disciplines into a fast, repeatable check -- not introducing new information, but making sure known disciplines are consistently applied before and during review.

questions.q: How does this lesson tie its conclusion back to Lesson 1's opening framing of the Application Architect role?
options: It argues Lesson 1's framing was incorrect and should be revised
It claims the Application Architect role is primarily about writing more Apex than a developer

It connects every mistake on the list back to Lesson 1's distinction between 'it works' and 'it's well-architected' -- each mistake is a way a solution can work short-term while failing the higher bar
It states that Lesson 1 and Lesson 25 cover entirely unrelated material
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly closes the loop with Lesson 1's 'it works' vs. 'it's well-architected' framing, showing each mistake as a way a solution passes the first bar while failing the second.
